text: Mari Lwyd was a Welsh folkloric figure. Between Christmas and January 6 an old hobbyhorse tradition was celebrated in villages throughout South Wales. The head of a horse, said to be the mare Mari Lwyd, was decorated with ribbons and other finery. A group carried the head from house to house. They demanded entry with obscure words and were answered with more verses from within. The horse and her carriers were finally admitted, whereupon celebrations followed. This trick-or-treating typically descends from earlier prophylactic rituals. The Mari Lwyd may have served as a ritual of safety and propitiation of cosmic powers for the year. The modern poet Dylan Thomas knew of this folklore, which inspired his Ballad of the Mari Lwyd.

okr.objective: Document Mari Lwyd, the Welsh hobbyhorse folkloric figure of the New Year season.
